messages:
ana (newhire): Morning team, second day and hitting weirdness. docker-compose up shows postgres starting then immediately 'FATAL: could not open file "/var/lib/postgresql/data/postgresql.conf": Permission denied'

ana (newhire): I ran compose with a host bind mount to ./pgdata to keep data between runs. On my Intel laptop this worked fine but my roommate with an M1 sees this error.

charlie: Welcome! On Mac the Docker Desktop VM manages filesystem permissions differently. Two paths: use a named Docker volume (recommended) or make sure the host dir permissions are wide open for testing. Example: `mkdir -p ./pgdata && chmod 0777 ./pgdata`

charlie: If you want to keep host dir, chown to the postgres uid in container: `docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/pgdata:/data alpine chown -R 999:999 /data`

ana (newhire): tried chmod 0777 but still same error. the chown trick worked, DB came up. thanks!

ralph: Also check that you don't have a background postgres on host using sockets. The error is permission on the file, but separate issue is socket vs tcp. Force TCP by setting `PGHOST=127.0.0.1` or using a DB url with host.

charlie: For CI parity, we keep compose overrides local only. Put local overrides in `docker-compose.local.yml` and add to .gitignore. CI uses docker-compose.ci.yml which uses named volumes so no host mount surprises.

devx-bot: https://redwood-inference.internal/docs/onboarding/local-services.md :point_right: "Local Postgres & Redis tips"

ana (newhire): great resource. one last question: redis persistence complaining about AOF lock when using host mount. any quick fix?

charlie: For redis, use a named volume or ensure lock file can be created. Example: `mkdir -p ./redis-data && chmod 0777 ./redis-data` or use `volumes: - redis-data:/data`

ana (newhire): done, all green. appreciate the quick help :clap:
